changes: Tithi normalized to trayodaśī (as written 'dvitṛyodsyā'; the 'dvi-' could be a stray syllable or dittography, noted)
Notes expanded: ŚS 989 (= 1067 CE) is impossible because the Sārasvata grammar postdates it, so NS 989 = 1869 CE is preferred; the catalogue era is wrong

notes: The catalogue gives the date as [ŚS] 989. That cannot be right: ŚS 989 is about 1067 CE, which is earlier than the Sārasvata grammar itself. A bare three-digit saṃvat in a Newari-script manuscript is Nepal Saṃvat, so NS 989 = c. 1869 CE (the month is Pauṣa, so this may fall in early 1870). 'va' = vadi, the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa). The tithi is written 'dvitṛyodsyā' and is read as trayodaśī, following the catalogue. The 'dvi-' may be a stray syllable, though dvitīyā cannot be ruled out. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris. The text is named in the colophon as 'śāśvatī vyākaraṇaprakriyā', probably a corruption of Sārasvatī. 'kaviḥ' is treated as a title (kavi).
